notes.decision: Translated 'the Awakener' — Lycopolitan ⲣⲉϥⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲥ = Sahidic ⲣⲉϥⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲥ, agentive ⲣⲉϥ- + ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲥ (causative of ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise/raise'). Standard Manichaean title for the Light-Mind, who awakens souls. Per the ⲧⲟⲩⲱ → 'raise' principle, 'Awakener' preserves the rising/raising directional sense (waking-up = causing to rise). Alternative parsing ⲣⲉϥ-ⲧⲟⲩⲛ-ⲛⲟⲩⲥ 'raiser of Mind' yields essentially the same meaning. The Five Sons of the Awakener correspond to the five intellectual faculties (ⲛⲟⲩⲥ, ⲙⲉⲩⲉ, ⲥⲃⲱ, ⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ, ⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ).

Translated 'drawer-upward' — ⲣⲉϥ- + ⲥⲱϩⲉ/ⲥⲁϩⲟ ('to draw, drag, pull') + ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ ('upward'). Preserves the upward/raising directional semantics consistent with the soteriology of light-particle elevation. The same root-pair appears in earlier vocabulary ⲭⲉⲥⲧ ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ ('convey upward'); here the form is closer to ⲥⲱϩⲉ. Each Son of the Awakener functions as a 'drawer-upward,' carrying souls/light from below toward the source.

notes.decision: Read as a continuation/second-part of the chapter heading: 'of those who died — the resurrection is at hand.' ⲁⲍⲁⲛ = ⲁϩⲏⲛ 'near, at hand'; ⲧⲉ = copula. The doubled ⲓ̄ⲅ (13) at start and end suggests decorative numeral framing. May indicate that chapter 13 has a compound topic: the Five Sons of the Awakener AND the dead at the time of resurrection.

Translated 'the foremost of them' — ⲙⲁϩ likely ordinal-prefix functioning as a substantive 'first/chief'; ⲛⲍⲏⲧϩ = ⲛϩⲏⲧⲟⲩ 'among them' (or ⲛϩⲏⲧϥ 'in him'). Given that lines 26, 28, 32 enumerate the second, third, fourth drawers-upward, this opening line should introduce the first.
Editorial sign ⳨ in this scribe's hand represents the ⲉⲓ ligature, confirmed by ⳨ⲣⲏⲛⲏ = εἰρήνη (line 14, 18) and ⲙⲡ⳨ⲟⲩ = ⲙⲡⲉⲓⲟⲩ (line 17). Preserved in coptic field.

Translated 'upward to the Good' on the assumption that editor's [ⲡ] should be read [ⲣ], giving Lycopolitan ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward' (= Sah. ⲉϩⲣⲁⲓ̈). The motion-toward-the-Good fits Manichaean ascent vocabulary; ⲁⲍⲡⲏⲓ̈ as such is unattested.
